readLimitedBody accumulated every chunk then allocated a SECOND full-body-sized Uint8Array to merge them into, so a near-cap request briefly held roughly 2x its own size in memory -- on the exact route meant to bound memory use. releaseReviewQueueReservation cleared resolver_reserved_until guarded only on the row being unresolved and unskipped, never on lease ownership. The lease could not round-trip: Postgres timestamptz keeps microseconds and the pg driver returns the column as a string (observed 2026-08-13 14:40:15.312121+00), while a JS Date holds milliseconds, so an untruncated lease came back as .312000 and the release predicate could never match its own row. Fixed by writing the lease through date_trunc('milliseconds', ...) so the value is exactly representable on both sides, plus an explicit string-to-Date conversion - Postgres's format uses a space separator and a two-digit offset (+00) that Node rejects outright.
